_comment: Form content for the 31 plan exercises (keyed by slug). regions use the 3D model's muscle vocabulary: chest_upper chest_lower delt_front delt_side delt_rear biceps triceps forearms lats mid_back traps lower_back abs glutes quads hamstrings calves.

flat-barbell-bench-press.description: The classic horizontal press for overall chest mass, with the front delts and triceps assisting.
cues: Lie with your eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades pinched together and down
Grip just wider than shoulder width with wrists stacked over elbows
Lower the bar under control to the lower chest with elbows about 45-60 degrees from your torso
Press up and slightly back toward the rack, keeping your glutes on the bench
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest
Flaring the elbows to 90 degrees, which stresses the shoulders
Lifting the hips or letting the shoulder blades slide forward
An uneven bar path, with one side rising faster
flat-barbell-bench-press.breathing: Breathe in and brace on the way down, then breathe out as you press past the sticking point.

incline-dumbbell-press.description: A press on a 30 to 45 degree bench that shifts the load to the upper chest and allows a deeper stretch than a bar.
cues: Set the bench to 30-45 degrees and kick the dumbbells up to the start position
Set your shoulder blades back and down before the first rep
Lower until your elbows are just below the bench line with forearms vertical
Press up and slightly in without clanging the dumbbells together
mistakes: Setting the bench so steep it becomes a shoulder press
Letting the dumbbells drift forward over your face
Cutting the range of motion short
incline-dumbbell-press.breathing: Breathe in on the way down, out as you press up.

cable-lower-chest-fly.description: A high-to-low cable fly that sweeps the arms down and across to isolate the lower chest fibres.
cues: Set the pulleys high and step forward into a staggered stance
Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows
Sweep your hands down and together toward your belly button, squeezing the lower chest
Return slowly until you feel a stretch across the chest, no further
mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows so it becomes a press
Using momentum from the torso
Letting the hands travel far behind the body line
cable-lower-chest-fly.breathing: Breathe out as your hands meet, in as the arms open.

seated-db-overhead-press.description: A seated dumbbell press that builds the front and side delts with a free path for each arm.
cues: Sit with your back supported, core braced and dumbbells at shoulder height
Press straight up until your arms are nearly locked, wrists stacked over elbows
Lower to about ear level with control
Keep your ribs down and avoid arching the lower back
mistakes: Excessive lower-back arch
Pressing forward instead of straight up
Letting the elbows flare far behind the torso
seated-db-overhead-press.breathing: Brace your core, then breathe out as you press.

side-lateral-raise.description: The main exercise for shoulder width: raise the arms out to the sides to load the side delts.
cues: Stand tall with soft knees and the dumbbells at your sides
Lead with the elbows and raise your arms out to shoulder height, not higher
Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout
Lower slowly over 2-3 seconds
mistakes: Swinging the torso to heave the weights up
Shrugging the traps toward the ears
Raising the arms above shoulder height
Using a weight that is too heavy
side-lateral-raise.breathing: Breathe out as you raise, in as you lower.

skull-crushers.description: A lying triceps extension that loads the long head of the triceps through a deep stretch.
cues: Lie on a bench with the bar over your chest and arms vertical
Keep your upper arms fixed, pointing slightly back over your head
Lower the bar toward your forehead by bending only at the elbows
Extend back up without letting the elbows flare wide
mistakes: Elbows drifting forward and out so it turns into a press
Going too heavy and cutting the range
Bending the wrists back under load
skull-crushers.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, out as you extend.

rope-tricep-pushdown.description: A cable pushdown for triceps isolation with a rope that lets the hands spread at the bottom.
cues: Stand close to the cable with a slight forward lean and elbows pinned to your sides
Push the rope down and spread the ends apart at the bottom
Squeeze the triceps, then return until your forearms are just past 90 degrees
Keep your shoulders down and still
mistakes: Elbows drifting forward or flaring out
Leaning over the weight and using body weight
Letting the weight stack slam at the top
rope-tricep-pushdown.breathing: Breathe out as you push down, in as you return.

barbell-row.description: A bent-over row that builds back thickness; the torso stays braced at a fixed hip hinge while the bar is pulled to the lower ribs.
cues: Hinge at the hips until your torso is about 30-45 degrees to the floor, back flat and knees soft
Grip just outside the knees with the bar starting over mid-foot
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs, driving the elbows back
Lower under control without changing your torso angle
mistakes: Rounding the lower back
Standing up as you pull and jerking the weight with the hips
Shrugging the bar up toward the chest
Craning the neck upward
barbell-row.breathing: Brace before each pull, breathe out as you pull, in as you lower.

lat-pulldown.description: A vertical pull on the cable that builds lat width. The wide-grip version on Friday spreads the grip beyond shoulder width.
cues: Sit with your thighs locked under the pads and grab the bar just wider than your shoulders
Lean back slightly and keep your chest up
Drive your elbows down toward your back pockets and bring the bar to the upper chest
Control the bar back up until your lats are fully stretched
mistakes: Pulling the bar behind the neck
Swinging the torso to move the weight
Pulling with the hands instead of the elbows
Letting the weight yank the shoulders up at the top
lat-pulldown.breathing: Breathe out as you pull down, in as the bar rises.

seated-cable-row.description: A horizontal cable row for mid-back thickness with constant tension through the full range.
cues: Sit tall with a slight knee bend, chest up and feet braced
Pull the handle to your lower ribs, squeezing the shoulder blades together
Pause briefly, then let the arms extend without rounding your back
Keep the torso still; a small lean is fine
mistakes: Rocking back and forth with momentum
Shrugging the shoulders
Rounding the lower back at the stretch
seated-cable-row.breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you extend.

straight-arm-pulldown.description: A straight-arm cable sweep that isolates the lats without the biceps taking over.
cues: Face the high cable with a slight hip hinge
Keep your arms nearly straight with a soft elbow bend
Sweep the bar down to your thighs by squeezing the lats
Control the bar back up to head height
mistakes: Bending the elbows so it becomes a pushdown
Leaning back and using momentum
Letting the bar travel behind the hips
straight-arm-pulldown.breathing: Breathe out as you sweep down, in as you return.

face-pull.description: A cable pull to the face for the rear delts and the small rotator-cuff muscles that keep the shoulders healthy.
cues: Set the rope at about face height
Pull toward your face, splitting the rope so your hands finish beside your ears
Keep your elbows high and rotate your thumbs back at the end
Control the return with your torso upright
mistakes: Pulling too low toward the chest
Leaning back and using body weight
Using so much weight the shoulders roll forward
face-pull.breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you return.

barbell-curl.description: The standard biceps mass builder: a strict standing curl with an underhand grip.
cues: Stand tall with a shoulder-width underhand grip and elbows tucked at your sides
Curl the bar up by bending only at the elbows
Squeeze at the top without letting the elbows drift forward
Lower for about 2-3 seconds
mistakes: Swinging the hips to cheat the weight up
Elbows travelling forward
Half reps at the bottom
Leaning back as you curl
barbell-curl.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.

dumbbell-hammer-curl.description: A neutral-grip curl that targets the brachialis and forearm muscles as well as the biceps.
cues: Keep your palms facing each other throughout
Pin your elbows to your ribs
Curl to shoulder height without twisting the wrists
Lower slowly under control
mistakes: Swinging the dumbbells
Letting the elbows move forward
Rushing the lowering phase
dumbbell-hammer-curl.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.

barbell-squat.description: The king of leg exercises: a full squat that builds overall leg mass and trains the whole trunk to brace.
cues: Set the bar on your upper back (not your neck), grip tight and brace your core
Stand with feet shoulder-width and toes slightly out, then sit down and back
Keep your knees tracking over your toes with the whole foot planted
Descend to at least parallel with a neutral spine, then drive up through the mid-foot
mistakes: Knees caving inward
Heels lifting or weight shifting onto the toes
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Folding forward over the bar
Cutting depth
barbell-squat.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before you descend, then breathe out after passing the sticking point.

leg-press.description: A machine press for quad volume with the back supported, so you can train hard without taxing your spine.
cues: Place your feet shoulder-width at mid-height on the platform
Lower until your knees are about 90 degrees, or as deep as your lower back stays flat on the pad
Press through the whole foot without locking out the knees hard
Keep your hips and lower back pressed into the seat
mistakes: Lower back peeling off the pad at the bottom
Locking out the knees forcefully
Knees caving in
Bouncing at the bottom
leg-press.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, out as you press.

romanian-deadlift.description: A hip hinge that loads the hamstrings and glutes through a long stretch with the bar close to the legs.
cues: Stand tall holding the bar at your hips with soft knees
Push your hips back as the bar slides down your thighs
Keep your back flat and shoulder blades set, stopping when you feel a deep hamstring stretch
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing the glutes
mistakes: Rounding the back
Squatting instead of hinging (too much knee bend)
Letting the bar drift away from the legs
Leaning back at the top
romanian-deadlift.breathing: Brace on the way down, breathe out as you stand.

hamstring-curl.description: A machine curl that isolates the hamstrings through a full range.
cues: Line your knee up with the machine pivot with the pad just above your heels
Curl smoothly toward your glutes
Squeeze the hamstrings at the top without lifting your hips
Return slowly over 2-3 seconds
mistakes: Hips lifting off the pad
Using momentum
Stopping short at the bottom
hamstring-curl.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.

leg-extension.description: A machine extension that isolates the quadriceps.
cues: Sit with your back against the pad and your knee in line with the pivot
Extend until your legs are almost straight, squeezing the quads
Pause for a second, then lower slowly
Keep your hips down in the seat
mistakes: Swinging the weight up with momentum
Hips rising off the seat
Slamming into a hard lockout
leg-extension.breathing: Breathe out as you extend, in as you lower.

standing-calf-raise.description: A loaded heel raise that trains the calves through a full stretch and contraction.
cues: Put the balls of your feet on the platform with your heels hanging off
Rise as high as you can onto your toes
Pause at the top, then lower into a deep stretch
Keep your knees nearly straight and move slowly
mistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom
A short range of motion
Rolling the ankles outward
standing-calf-raise.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, in as you lower.

arnold-press.description: A rotating dumbbell press that hits the front, side and rear delts in one movement.
cues: Start with the dumbbells in front of your chest, palms facing you
As you press up, rotate your palms to face forward
Finish with your arms nearly straight overhead
Reverse the rotation as you lower
mistakes: Arching the lower back
Rushing the rotation
Flaring the elbows too early
arnold-press.breathing: Breathe out as you press, in as you lower.

reverse-pec-deck-rear-delts.description: A reverse fly on the pec-deck machine that isolates the rear delts.
cues: Rest your chest on the pad with the handles at shoulder height and a slight bend in the elbows
Sweep your arms back and out in a wide arc
Squeeze the rear delts without shrugging
Return under control without letting the weights rest
mistakes: Pulling with the arms and shrugging
Rocking the torso
Setting the handles too low or too high
reverse-pec-deck-rear-delts.breathing: Breathe out as you sweep back, in as you return.

incline-bench-press.description: A barbell press on a 30 degree bench for upper-chest development.
cues: Set the bench to about 30 degrees with your eyes under the bar and shoulder blades set
Lower to the upper chest with your elbows about 45-60 degrees from the torso
Press up and slightly back
Keep your glutes on the bench and feet planted
mistakes: Setting the bench too steep
Bouncing the bar off the chest
Bending the wrists back
An uneven lockout
incline-bench-press.breathing: Breathe in and brace on the way down, out as you press.

butterfly-machine.description: A machine fly that squeezes the chest with constant tension.
cues: Set the seat so the handles are at chest height with your back flat against the pad
Keep a slight bend in the elbows and bring the handles together in front of your chest
Squeeze for a second
Return until you feel a gentle stretch, not past the shoulder line
mistakes: Letting the shoulders roll forward
Using momentum
Using too much weight and cutting the range
butterfly-machine.breathing: Breathe out as the handles meet, in as they open.

cable-overhead-tricep-extension.description: An overhead cable extension that stretches and loads the long head of the triceps.
cues: Face away from the cable with the rope behind your head and elbows pointing forward
Take a small lunge stance for stability with your upper arms close to your ears
Extend your arms overhead by straightening only the elbows
Return to a deep stretch behind your head
mistakes: Flaring the elbows wide
Arching the lower back
Moving the upper arms instead of keeping them fixed
cable-overhead-tricep-extension.breathing: Breathe out as you extend, in as you return.

reverse-grip-tricep-pushdown.description: An underhand-grip pushdown that biases the outer head of the triceps.
cues: Use an underhand grip on a straight or EZ bar
Pin your elbows to your sides
Push down until your arms are straight, squeezing the outer triceps
Return slowly until your forearms are just past 90 degrees
mistakes: Elbows drifting forward
Bending the wrists back
Using body weight to move the stack
reverse-grip-tricep-pushdown.breathing: Breathe out as you push down, in as you return.

pull-ups-assisted-pull-ups.description: A bodyweight vertical pull for lat width and strength. Use a band or assist machine until you can do full reps unassisted.
cues: Hang from the bar with a grip slightly wider than your shoulders and shoulders pulled down
Drive your elbows down and back, leading with the chest
Pull until your chin clears the bar
Lower to a full hang under control
mistakes: Kipping or swinging
Half reps that never reach a full hang
Jutting the chin forward without the chest rising
Shrugging the shoulders at the bottom
pull-ups-assisted-pull-ups.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up, in as you lower.

single-arm-dumbbell-row.description: A one-arm row braced on a bench that builds back thickness and corrects left/right imbalances.
cues: Place one hand and knee on the bench with your back flat and parallel to the floor
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip with the elbow close to your body
Squeeze the shoulder blade back at the top
Lower fully with control and no twisting of the torso
mistakes: Rotating the torso to heave the weight
Pulling toward the chest with the elbow flared
Rounding the back
single-arm-dumbbell-row.breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you lower.

shrugs-db-or-barbell.description: A simple lift that builds the upper traps, using dumbbells or a barbell.
cues: Stand tall with the weight at your sides or in front of your thighs
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears
Pause and squeeze the traps at the top
Lower slowly to a full stretch
mistakes: Rolling the shoulders, which adds joint stress and no benefit
Bending the elbows to help the lift
Jutting the head forward
shrugs-db-or-barbell.breathing: Breathe out as you shrug, in as you lower.

spider-curl.description: A curl done chest-down on an incline bench so the arms hang straight, which removes swing and strongly contracts the biceps peak.
cues: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight down
Curl the weight up, keeping your upper arms vertical
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top
Lower until your arms are fully extended
mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench
Swinging the upper arms backward
Using momentum
spider-curl.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.

preacher-curl.description: A curl over a preacher pad that isolates the lower biceps by removing any help from the shoulders.
cues: Rest your armpits snug against the top of the pad with your upper arms flat on it
Curl up without lifting your elbows
Lower slowly to just short of full lockout to protect the elbow
Keep your wrists straight
mistakes: Dropping fast into full extension, which strains the elbow
Lifting the elbows or hips off the pad
Using too much weight and a partial range
preacher-curl.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.
